clue.text: She's the sort always ready to needle.

definitions.text: She's the sort always ready to needle.

parts.words: She's the sort always ready to needle.
parts.note: to needle sounds like teasing someone, but here the woman literally plies a needle for her trade

explanation.definitionFit: A seamstress who sews for a living is always at work with a needle and thread.

clue.text: Likely to be soft, these concessions.

definitions.text: Likely to be soft, these concessions.

parts.words: Likely to be soft, these concessions.
parts.note: small concessions offered to placate someone are also, literally, pieces of bread soaked soft in liquid

explanation.definitionFit: Placating gifts take their name from bread dipped in broth, which is naturally soggy.

clue.text: Threats from fellows: with 8 dn's suits?

parts.note: fellows means men
the solution at 8 down is a master card, and in each suit the ace is the top card

explanation.surface: A question of whether men holding the best cards in every suit pose a danger at the table.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue leans on the answer to 8 down: the aces are the master cards of the four suits.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural synonym: intimidating warnings or dangers that loom over someone.

clue.text: You'll get it, as a matter of course, they're off!

definitions.text: You'll get it, as a matter of course, they're off!

parts.words: You'll get it, as a matter of course, they're off!
parts.note: the racecourse cry when horses leave the stalls; the odds fixed at that moment are what a punter is paid

explanation.walkthrough: 'Course' is the racecourse, not 'naturally'; in British betting the odds on offer as the race begins settle untaken bets.
explanation.definitionFit: Betting term for the odds prevailing when a horse race actually begins.

clue.text: Presumably one who can take it.

definitions.text: Presumably one who can take it.

parts.words: Presumably one who can take it.
parts.note: someone who can take it sounds tough, but here they simply accept what is handed over, perhaps stolen goods

explanation.definitionFit: One who accepts or takes delivery of something, including a fence handling stolen property.

clue.text: This gives a full indication (not a cram).

definitions.text: This gives a full indication (not a cram).

parts.words: This gives a full indication (not a cram).
parts.note: a vessel filled to its upper edge is full, a measure of fullness rather than an overstuffed cram

explanation.definitionFit: The rim of a cup or glass marks when it is full to the top.

clue.text: Yet another collection coming to ruin one

indicators.note: letters of ruin and one, when they come to something, regroup into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gathering doomed to end in disaster for someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A gathering again of people previously assembled, such as old classmates.

clue.text: Really top-class wag, good for any trick.

parts.note: a master is someone really top-class at a craft
a card is a joker, a wag

explanation.surface: Praise for a brilliant joker who can pull off any prank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trick' is a prank in the surface, but in card games it is a round won by the highest card.
explanation.definitionFit: In whist or bridge, the highest remaining card in a suit is certain to take any round it is played to.

clue.text: It takes a middleman to bring the peace-maker to earth

parts.note: to inter is to bury, to put in the earth
a mediator makes peace between parties

explanation.surface: A broker is needed to bring a mediator down to the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A go-between who acts on behalf of two parties.

clue.text: Risky procedure calling for an chopper ?

clue.text: Contents of 'cops' charts may well make one peeved.

indicators.note: the letters of cops and charts may well make something else when rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Police maps that leave someone grumpy.
explanation.definitionFit: A bad-tempered, irritable person, a grouch.

clue.text: Cancel everything

parts.note: to cancel completely, wiping out all that was agreed

explanation.definitionFit: An emphatic form of the verb to annul: to make void altogether.

clue.text: Maybe her pa's little angel?

indicators.note: maybe suggests the letters could be arranged otherwise

parts.note: taken as written
the possessive keeps its S as a letter here

explanation.surface: A father's darling daughter described as his little angel.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the highest order of heavenly beings in angelic hierarchy.

clue.text: They have, without doubt, disturbing effect.

definitions.text: They have, without doubt, disturbing effect.

parts.words: They have, without doubt, disturbing effect.
parts.note: the disturbance is literal: people breaking the peace in the streets

explanation.definitionFit: People who take part in a violent public disturbance.

clue.text: Board man, hardly the sandwich type!

definitions.text: Board man, hardly the sandwich type!

parts.words: Board man, hardly the sandwich type!
parts.note: a member of a company's board, not a man walking the street between two advertising boards

explanation.walkthrough: A sandwich-board man carries advertising boards front and back; this board is a company's governing body.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the governing body of a company.

clue.text: Yes, the glass seems likely to fall.

definitions.text: Yes, the glass seems likely to fall.

parts.words: Yes, the glass seems likely to fall.
parts.note: a drinking glass whose name suggests it is prone to toppling over

explanation.definitionFit: A flat-bottomed drinking glass, named because early ones had rounded bases and toppled.

clue.text: Typical, this, of local gossip.

parts.note: narrow small-town attitudes and talk, characteristic of those outside the capital

explanation.definitionFit: Narrowness of outlook associated with life in the regions away from the metropolis.

clue.text: Act, the goat? Well, dance like one.

definitions.meaning: to act the goat is to fool about, frolic
to skip and leap about playfully, as a goat does

explanation.definitionFit: A playful leap or prank; the word comes from Latin for goat.

clue.text: Past this, it's quite bucolic — so to speak.

definitions.text: Past this, it's quite bucolic — so to speak.

parts.words: Past this, it's quite bucolic — so to speak.
parts.note: put 'past' before the word and you hear a term for rustic country life; the word itself means spoken

explanation.definitionFit: Spoken rather than written, which is what 'so to speak' points at.

clue.text: Eftsoons!

parts.note: an archaic word meaning soon afterwards, at once

explanation.definitionFit: Both are old-fashioned ways of saying immediately after that.

clue.text: No, he's not responsible for a range hats.

definitions.text: No, he's not responsible for a range hats.

parts.words: No, he's not responsible for a range hats.
parts.note: 'tile' is slang for a hat, but this tradesman lays roof tiles, not hats

explanation.walkthrough: 'Tile' is old slang for a hat, so a maker of tiles could be a hatter; really he covers roofs.
explanation.definitionFit: A workman who lays tiles on roofs, floors or walls.
